data.narrative:
Anatar is a Series C robotics and manufacturing company founded by Kaia Rhodes. Valuation analysis draws on a comparable company universe of nine private firms and one public entity (277810.KQ) operating in the same sector and stage band. The peer set includes later-stage companies like Exotec ($2.0B, Series D) and Hadrian ($1.6B, Series D), as well as earlier-stage peers including Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B, Series B) and Dexterity ($1.6B, Series B).

The peer-median methodology, the single applicable triangulation approach given available data, yields an implied valuation of $1.6B across a seven-company cohort filtered for sector and stage alignment. The peer universe ranges from $1.0B to $2.0B, reflecting material dispersion across the robotics and manufacturing landscape even within adjacent stages.

Synthesizing this single-method analysis, Anatar's valuation range is supported at $1.4B (low), $1.6B (median), and $1.9B (high). Key uncertainties include: the absence of revenue multiples or growth-rate adjustments specific to Anatar; stage-to-stage valuation step-ups (Series C pricing relative to the Series B and D peers in the set); and differentiation factors not captured by peer multiples. A second valuation method would materially strengthen conviction in this range.
